a question of having credit with God. This is only apparently
true, for in reality every man, whether he cares to admit it
or not, is in the last resort concerned about his standing
before God. For why does he wish to be recognized and dis-
tinguished by other men? At bottom not because he attaches
so much importance to other men and their opinions; he
may despise them even while hankering after their recogni-
tion. At bottom he needs their appreciation because he
wishes to be certain of himself. In the last analysis every man
feels that his existence is of questionable and dubious value;
there lurks in the mind of every man the fear of nothingness
and the void, and the fear that it may also be true of him
to say: "Weighed in the balances and found wanting." And
the life of men consists largely in the effort to delude oneself
about these inner realities, and to suppress these fears. Man
tries to do this by various means, and it is this very thing
which he is trying to do in his search for recognition and
prestige. Being aware of the emptiness of his inner life,
he clings to the picture that others form of him. In this
picture he as it were sees himself mirrored, he holds fast to
it, and views in it the reflection of his true self. And just for
this reason the picture must be as great and imposing as
possible. In essence it is not in the eyes of others that he
wishes to stand out as great, but in his own eyes; in essence he
wishes to enjoy credit not before others but before himself.
Before himself! And that in the last resort means before
God. It is God who faces him with this pressing question,
whether he has something to show or whether he has lived
in vain and worthlessly. He feels that he is responsible for his
being and that he is called to make something of it. All
human longing for recognition is ultimately aimed at
providing an answer to that decisive question: am I,
generally speaking, a creature of worth or am I worthless?
Now of course it can make a great deal of difference whether
and to what an extent a man reckons with God in his life or
not. If a man no longer recognizes God as the controlling
